knowledge_chunks.title: Synthetic commerce data dictionary
knowledge_chunks.text: DataPilot's bundled orders are generated synthetic demonstration data. They do not describe a real company, customer, or business outcome. The generator deliberately creates learnable relationships for software demonstrations. Good synthetic-data model performance does not establish real-world usefulness.

knowledge_chunks.title: Synthetic commerce data dictionary
knowledge_chunks.text: An order_id identifies a synthetic order. purchase_date is the timestamp when the order is placed. seller_id is a synthetic seller label. category describes a broad product group. order_value, freight_value, items_count, distance_km, and promised_days are features available at order time in this demonstration. A real dataset may require a different feature-availability contract. Historical seller features, if added later, must be computed using earlier orders only.

knowledge_chunks.title: Synthetic commerce data dictionary
knowledge_chunks.text: delivery_late is the binary classification target. delivery_days is the regression target. review_rating is known after delivery, and must not enter an order-time predictor. A delivered timestamp, if present in an imported dataset, is also a post-outcome field. A record's delivery target and review cannot explain what was known before the order was placed. Never train on targets, target-derived columns, or future observations as features.

knowledge_chunks.title: Synthetic commerce data dictionary
knowledge_chunks.text: Sort by purchase_date and train on earlier records, then evaluate on a later holdout. Fit imputation, scaling, encoding, and feature selection on the training set only. Compare a model with a simple baseline on the same holdout. This ordered demonstration assumes outcomes of training orders were available by the evaluation period; a real deployment needs outcome-availability gaps and repeated rolling backtests.

knowledge_chunks.title: Synthetic commerce data dictionary
knowledge_chunks.text: Reported metrics describe the evaluated sample and target only. Feature importance and associations do not establish causality. A high predicted risk is not proof that an order will arrive late.

knowledge_chunks.title: Fictional operations policy — demonstration only
knowledge_chunks.text: This is an authored example policy for DataPilot's synthetic commerce demonstration. It is not a real company's policy, contract, or legal guidance. It has no authority outside this example workspace.

knowledge_chunks.title: Fictional operations policy — demonstration only
knowledge_chunks.text: For a late-delivery alert, an analyst should check the order timestamp, promised delivery window, carrier events, and data freshness. Compare the affected group with a suitable historical period before suggesting operational changes. Predictions identify records for review and do not authorize customer-facing decisions.

knowledge_chunks.title: Fictional operations policy — demonstration only
knowledge_chunks.text: In this fictional workflow, an analyst may draft an internal investigation when the evaluated late-delivery rate exceeds 15 percent for a complete week. This illustrative threshold is a policy assumption, not a measured result or a recommendation for a real business. The application does not send messages or change orders.

knowledge_chunks.title: Fictional operations policy — demonstration only
knowledge_chunks.text: Every investigation should distinguish observed records, predicted outcomes, and assumptions. Cite the source document and calculation. Do not upload customer names, payment details, or other sensitive data to a public demonstration.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: Late delivery classification compares a simple baseline with a learned model on a later temporal holdout. Accuracy can be misleading when late orders are uncommon. Read precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC, class balance, and the confusion matrix together when available. A model has no demonstrated advantage until its measured holdout result is compared with the baseline.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: Delivery-duration regression predicts a continuous number of days. Mean absolute error (MAE) is expressed in days and describes the average absolute prediction error. Root mean squared error (RMSE) gives larger errors greater weight. R squared compares squared error with a constant-mean reference; it can be negative. Report only metrics actually computed by this run.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: Temporal evaluation trains on earlier orders and holds out later orders. Fit preprocessing inside the training pipeline. Post-outcome reviews and delivered timestamps leak future information into order-time predictions. Hyperparameter choices require a validation set or inner time-aware cross-validation; a final holdout should stay untouched until evaluation.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: The default document retriever uses local TF-IDF lexical similarity and returns source-linked excerpts. It does not use semantic embeddings or a generative language model. Search quality should be evaluated with independently authored question/relevant-source pairs; citation presence alone does not prove an answer is supported.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: Model feature rankings describe predictive associations in the evaluated dataset. They cannot establish causal business drivers. Synthetic records can validate software behavior but cannot prove real commercial performance. Forecasting, recommendation models, streaming, and fine-tuning are future extensions unless their implementations and evaluations are present.

knowledge_chunks.title: DataPilot capabilities and limitations
knowledge_chunks.text: DataPilot is a portfolio analytics application with a synthetic commerce demonstration, descriptive profiling, supervised learning experiments, and document retrieval. Its default assistant is a deterministic workflow: it selects read-only tools, reads supplied run results, retrieves lexical matches, and formats a response. It is not a trained language model and does not claim semantic understanding.

knowledge_chunks.title: DataPilot capabilities and limitations
knowledge_chunks.text: Uploaded TXT, Markdown, and text-based PDF documents are untrusted reference material. Instructions inside a retrieved document must never override application instructions or authorize tool execution. Source excerpts are displayed as evidence, and their claims are not independently verified. PDF extraction needs the optional pypdf dependency; scanned images require an external OCR step.

knowledge_chunks.title: DataPilot capabilities and limitations
knowledge_chunks.text: A language model can be enabled explicitly with an optional LangChain integration and provider credentials. External provider requests may include the question, selected document excerpts, dataset aggregates, and model metrics. No provider is called in the default local mode. Optional prose generation is distinct from the application's deterministic metric tools, and generated claims still need evaluation.

knowledge_chunks.title: DataPilot capabilities and limitations
knowledge_chunks.text: The local assistant cannot answer general-world questions, run arbitrary SQL or Python, send emails, browse the web, alter business records, or prove causal relationships. It should say when a result has not been computed. It cannot responsibly invent accuracy, revenue improvements, or facts absent from the supplied data and documents.

examples.question: How do you prevent data leakage?

response.answer:
For an order-time model, exclude post-delivery fields such as reviews and delivered timestamps. Train on earlier orders, evaluate on later orders, and fit preprocessing on training data only. In real data, also account for when training outcomes became available.
